review_cost.rationale: Approve-with-nits: everything works, matches current framework practice and the spec; the handful of comments I'd leave (internal flag, dead code, duplicate call, URL sync) are all one-line fixes.

findings.issue: Card sprites are constructed from a hardcoded URL pattern instead of consuming the API-provided sprites.front_default URL; if the media layout ever diverges from the documented pattern, every card breaks.
findings.suggestion: Either add a short comment citing the spec's guaranteed pattern, or thread front_default through CardData where it's already available.

findings.issue: '<n> of 6' counts cookie entries (team.length) while cards and coverage come from the server's resolved members; a cookie entry the API doesn't have makes the count, card list and coverage disagree.
findings.suggestion: Render the count from data.members.length (or reconcile client team against server members) so all three stay consistent.

findings.issue: Cache eviction only removes already-expired entries, so the >5000 guard never bounds growth when all entries are fresh.
findings.suggestion: Drop the oldest entries (by insertion order) when the cap is exceeded, or cap per-namespace.

findings.issue: head() relies on the internal m._notFound match flag in addition to the public m.status === 'notFound'.
findings.suggestion: Use only the public status field.

findings.issue: getTeamPage awaits typeList() twice (second call immediately followed by per-type getType); redundant even though memoized.
findings.suggestion: Call typeList() once and derive both the label list and the per-type fetches from it.

findings.issue: readTeamCookie (and standalone encodeTeam) are exported but never used — dead code.
findings.suggestion: Delete readTeamCookie, or inline encodeTeam into writeTeamCookie.

findings.issue: document.cookie write happens inside the setTeam updater function — a side effect in a state reducer that React may double-invoke under StrictMode.
findings.suggestion: Compute the next team outside the updater, then setTeam(next) and writeTeamCookie(next) in the event handler.

findings.issue: The displayed page is clamped to totalPages but the URL keeps the stale ?page value, so 'Previous page'/'Next page' links can navigate from a page the URL doesn't reflect.
findings.suggestion: When clamping differs from search.page, replace the URL with the clamped page.

findings.issue: Row keys `${row.move}-${row.level}` can collide if the API lists the same move twice for one method+game at the same level.
findings.suggestion: Include the row index in the key.

findings.issue: No errorComponent: an API failure surfaces as the framework's default error UI rather than an app-styled one.
findings.suggestion: Add a small shared errorComponent alongside NotFound.

summary: A well-organized, current-generation TanStack Start app: canonical server functions (including the post-2026 validator API), idiomatic routing/search handling, disciplined server/client boundaries and SSR-correct cookie-backed team state. All findings are minor edge cases and clean-up nits — dead exports, a duplicate call, weak cache eviction, and small URL/key inconsistencies. I'd approve after one quick pass fixing the nits.
